title: My workflow saves you 20 hours a month.
subtitle: The previous 5 lessons compose into a repeatable sequence. Here it is, all at once.

Let's go.

paragraphs: The title says 20 hours a month. It's not hyperbole.
Stefano measured it on himself. 20 hours a month recovered, out of 80 hours of monthly vibe coding. A quarter of his productive life.
How? No magic. Just method. I'll explain right now.

vignettes.full: 20 is the real number, measured over months. Not a landing-page claim.
Measure, don't say. Keep it as an operational rule.

paragraphs: The beginner vibe coder opens the laptop, fires up the AI, and dives in. «Let's see what happens».
Result: 4 hours just to figure out what they were doing. 2 hours fixing errors they created themselves. 1 hour rebuilding the pieces they broke.
The serious vibe coder does something different: they think for 5 minutes before writing the first prompt. Those 5 minutes save them the 7 hours.

vignettes.full: 5 minutes vs 7 hours. It's math, not opinion.
It's math. Re-read this tomorrow before opening Cursor.

steps.headline: The workflow
steps.caption: Techniques alone aren't enough. It's the workflow — the repeatable sequence of actions — that multiplies everything. Without a workflow you know the notes but you don't play the song.

vignettes.full: Notes without a song. Nice to hear, gets you nowhere.
Now we compose them in your head. Becomes instinct in two weeks.

paragraphs: The workflow has 4 phases. I'll list them — easy to remember.
1. SETUP. One-time configuration: CLAUDE.md, [[term:repository]]repository[[/term]], tools. Once and done.
2. KICKOFF. At the start of every session, give the AI what it needs.
3. EXECUTION. The real work: prompt, constraints, iteration.
4. VERIFICATION. End of session: tests, [[term:code-review]]code review[[/term]], [[term:commit]]commit[[/term]]. Never skip it.
Four phases, always in the same order. Becomes instinct in two weeks.

One counter-intuitive thing about phase 3, then we're done. Most people put constraints **after** the task: «do X, but don't do Y». Sounds logical. It's wrong — I read in sequence, and by the time I get to constraints I'm already mentally elsewhere.
Flip the order. **Constraints before the task.** I work inside the frame, I don't discover it after.
The perfect prompt is: CONTEXT → CONSTRAINTS → TASK → VERIFICATION. I'll have you build it at the end.

vignettes.full: Sounds odd the first time. Try it, then you don't go back.
Try it tomorrow. It works, I promise.
This is the fifth mental reversal of Path 1. Keep it close — few people know it.

steps.prompt: Which of these 4 phases do you think is the MOST neglected by beginner vibe coders?

options.label: Setup — they don't configure a CLAUDE.md.
Kickoff — they dive in without giving the AI any info.
Verification — they don't check what the AI actually did.

vignettes.full: Think before clicking. One of these costs the most, and it's the one that gets skipped most.

paragraphs: Got it. Moving on.

Keep this in mind: verification is the phase everyone skips, and it's the one that costs the most. The AI says «done», they close. Tomorrow they find the bug, and they have to remember what they were doing. Result: they start over.

steps.headline: Vibe coding
steps.caption: You know the techniques. You know the workflow. Now you have to make it instinct. Two weeks of consistent practice. Then you don't think about it. You just do it.

vignettes.full: Two weeks of consistent practice. Nothing more, nothing less.
Nothing more, nothing less. Promise.

paragraphs: Let me tell you how Stefano does it. A day of vibe coding on Promptly.
**8:30** — Opens Cursor. Re-reads the CLAUDE.md (15 seconds). Remembers the project's state.
**8:35** — Writes the first prompt of the day. Context up top, constraints right after, task last. Verification asked explicitly inside the prompt.
**8:45** — Execution. Iterates 3-4 times on the prompt until the AI gets it. Never accepts the first response that «seems ok».
**10:30** — Break. Verification: reads the [[term:diff]]diff[[/term]], runs the tests, commits with a clear message.
**11:00** — New cycle. Same sequence.
Sounds boring. It is. And that's exactly why it works.

vignettes.full: Operational boredom is a superpower. You only notice it after a few weeks.
Chaos is the enemy. You avoid it with method, nothing more.

paragraphs: Now I'll have you build YOUR daily prompt. The one you open every morning before you start vibe coding.

I'll give you 4 pillars to arrange in the right order — the counter-intuitive one I just taught you. When it's done, you'll see them transform into a real, complete prompt you can use TOMORROW morning in your session. You can even download it as a .md file.
No theory. Just construction.

vignettes.full: No fill the gap. It's real construction, with your own hands.
Real construction. You take it home for real.

paragraphs: PS: the prompt you'll build in a moment, paste it at the start of every vibe-coding session. Your tool will keep it as a context anchor for the whole work.
Keep the .md file handy. You only edit the TASK of the day. Everything else stays the same, always.

vignettes.full: One file, a thousand sessions. It's your operational compass.

paragraphs: Path 1 closed.

You learned that the AI executes and you direct. You set up the configuration. You understood context. You set the constraints — before the task, please. You learned to read errors. You composed the workflow.
Remember when I asked you, on the first lesson, why you were here? You told me: «{deep_motivation}».
That still holds. Actually it holds even more now, because you have the tools to actually make it.
Path 2 is called «Build». I take you from «I can direct the AI» to «I can build and ship a real product». But that's for next time.
Now, party. You've earned the sweetest 5-minute break of all.

vignettes.full: You've become serious. Few make it here.
Few make it here. You did.
See you soon, vibe coder. When you come back, I'll be ready.
